A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rex research work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–K. Retained content can be matched across the substantial reorganization, including the relocated interpolation experiment.

before.justification: V2 reports original image-generation measurements, FRLL interpolation examples, solver ablations, and inversion failure analyses in Section 5 and Appendices J–K.

after.justification: V3 retains original image-generation results and reports additional image-editing and tri-alanine sampling experiments, including a trained DiT model, in Section 4.

M1.justification: The coupled Rex updates, Lawson/(S)RK construction, and Brownian-path reuse in v2 Proposition 3.3 are retained in v3 Appendix C.3 and the code illustrations. Princeps names the existing underlying solver; the Dopri5 experiments instantiate the already general solver family.

E1.justification: V3 adds instruction-based editing on InstructPix2Pix and equilibrium conformation sampling of tri-alanine. CelebA-HQ generation, COCO-conditioned generation, and FRLL interpolation remain; interpolation moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix K.2.

E2.justification: The new Boltzmann comparison in v3 Table 4 includes RegFlow, SBG with IS and SMC, ECNF++, and DiT with conventional Dopri5. Existing image-generation comparisons retain DDIM, EDICT, BDIA, and O-BELM; the additional BDIA row changes its coupling setting.

E3.justification: V3 replaces Inception-based FID with DINOv2 FD, FD∞, precision, recall, density, and coverage, and adds PickScore. It evaluates an additional BDIA coupling setting. New protocols include 100 editing examples with 100 fixed steps and adaptive Dopri5 tolerances of 10^-5 for Boltzmann sampling.

E4.justification: V2's full unconditional base-solver ablation loses its Euler and ShARK entries; v3 Table 1 retains comparisons among Midpoint, RK4, and Euler-Maruyama under new metrics. V3 adds a BDIA coupling comparison and reweighting diagnostics in Figure 5. Appendix J's inversion failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: V3 adds FD∞ bias estimation by fitting FD across 15 sample counts in Appendix I.1.2. Fixed-seed reporting remains, without new repeated-run variability estimates or confidence intervals. The new 1% boldface rule is a ranking convention, not an uncertainty interval.

E6.justification: V3 replaces the FID results with measurements under different metrics, retains the existing Table 2 CLIP/Image Reward values, and adds PickScore, another BDIA configuration, editing results, and Boltzmann results. In the new DiT comparison, Rex gives E-W2 0.495 versus 0.737, but ESS 0.104 versus 0.140 and T-W2 0.497 versus 0.468.

T1.justification: V3 adds generalized SDE Proposition 3.1, unified ODE Proposition C.1 and their derivations, and OT-flow inverse formulas. Existing convergence and solver-equivalence results largely remain. The new SDE proof requires g²=bΞ in Equations 130–131, which does not follow from its stated assumption g²=ab.

C1.justification: V3 makes improved Boltzmann sampling through invertibility and quantitative image-editing performance central contributions, broadening v2's generation/interpolation emphasis. High-order ODE convergence and exact SDE inversion claims remain. The prominently presented solver-subsumption claim already appeared in v2 Appendix E.

C2.justification: V3 adds the argument that numerical invertibility supports valid likelihood calculations for Boltzmann reweighting, and explains choosing ζ=0.001 when actual inversion is unnecessary. It interprets energy-distance gains alongside ESS and torsional-distance tradeoffs. The earlier latent-instability limitations remain in Appendix J.

D1.justification: V3 adds printed Rex forward/backward and ShARK code, OT-flow schedule formulas, explicit baseline hyperparameters, DiT architecture and training details, and additional metric/dataset repository pointers. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the H100 hardware and torchsde Brownian-interval disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V3 expands positioning into Boltzmann generators and DINOv2/human-preference evaluation, with corresponding new references and discussion. Appendix A.1.4 adds a substantive comparison with Shmelev and Salvi's approximately reversible schemes. The earlier DDIM, DPM-Solver, and SEEDS relationships remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and method narrative are substantially rewritten around the Princeps-to-Rex recipe. Preliminaries are reordered, theory becomes Section 3.3, a main related-work section appears, and interpolation moves to the appendix. Implementation material is reorganized and a code appendix added.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document template, theorem styling, diagrams, and table structures. It adds editing and Boltzmann tables, energy-distribution plots, and an architecture table. Existing image-example panels are retained, while the interpolation figure moves to Appendix K and the unconditional ablation table disappears.

improvement.justification: Quantitative editing and Boltzmann experiments strengthen application evidence, and the code and training details improve documentation. However, the new central SDE generalization contains a substantive proof gap: Proposition 3.1 assumes g²=ab, while Equations 130–131 require g²=bΞ without establishing it. These empirical and reproducibility gains coexist with weakened theoretical reliability, leaving the overall net improvement uncertain.
